subject: Leadership post-call: value hypotheses, procurement path, escalation items
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lewis <samantha.lewis@healthmatrix.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@healthmatrix.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-30T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Leadership post-call: value hypotheses, procurement path, escalation items

Samantha / Raj — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side so we have shared alignment and clear next steps for leadership at HealthMatrix. I tried to capture the business outcomes, the key risks you raised, and a pragmatic procurement path. Please flag anything I missed.

Top-level business outcomes you’re aiming for (as discussed):
- Reduce average claims processing time by 40% in under 6 months (target metric: median processing latency).
- Improve triage accuracy for high-priority claims to reduce manual review volume by 30%.
- Maintain or improve customer-facing SLA for claim status updates while lowering per-transaction inference cost.

Confirmed pain points / decision drivers we heard:
1) Latency variance on peak days — current API bursts cause backlogs and manual escalations.
2) Cost predictability — procurement wants a clear unit-cost model and visibility into burst charges.
3) Data residency & auditability — internal auditors will require detailed access logs and proof of deletion for PII that touches the model.
4) Quality regressions — the analytics team needs a way to detect and roll back model-quality regressions tied to prompt changes.

Primary risks (leadership-level):
- Procurement timeline: finance needs a 60–90 day window for SOW and PO.
- Security gating: SOC2 Type II evidence + KMS integration are hard stops for private deployment.
- Integration effort: Claims platform runs a mix of on-prem ETL and cloud microservices — we estimate ~4 weeks of integration work for a minimal POC.

Proposed procurement path (suggested, flexible):
1) 2-week technical POC scoped to a narrow claims flow (sample of high-volume endpoints) — objective: measure latency and end-to-end cost per claim.
2) Security & legal questionnaire sprint (we’ll provide targeted artifacts): SOC2 summary, network diagram, data flow, and KMS options.
3) Executive review + approve SOW for 3-month pilot with reserved capacity (discounted pilot pricing) and exit criteria defined.
4) Post-pilot: scaled reserved capacity + 12–18 month contract if pilot meets latency and cost targets.

Immediate asks / next steps: 
- HealthMatrix: commit to dates for security kickoff and procurement kickoff (finance contact and PO window).
- Redwood: share the redacted SOC2 bundle, an example private deployment network diagram, and a pilot MAP (Milestones/Acceptance/Price) — I attached a draft MAP and the security checklist we discussed.
- Point people: Aditya (Redwood) will lead POC; Marissa will own SRE onboarding; Neha will coordinate legal artifacts.

Timeline suggestion (high-level):
- Week 0–2: finalize POC scope and sign mutual NDA/APP (if needed)
- Week 3–6: run POC (measurement window: 2 weeks)
- Week 7: exec review of pilot results + procurement decision

Escalation path: if SOC2 / KMS gating delays contract beyond 90 days, propose an interim hosted environment with additional contractual safeguards and audit logging to bridge compliance needs.

Attachments: HealthMatrix-Security-Requirements.pdf (security checklist), HealthMatrix-draft-MAP.xlsx (proposed pilot milestones & pricing).

If this captures things correctly I’ll move to schedule the security kickoff and drop a calendar invite for the POC planning session.

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Samantha Lewis <samantha.lewis@healthmatrix.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@healthmatrix.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-30T17:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Leadership post-call: value hypotheses, procurement path, escalation items

Aditya — this is helpful, thank you. Couple of clarifications from our side: 
- The 40% reduction target is ambitious but directionally correct — execs will want a credible baseline and the sensitivity if we adjust to a 25–35% target.
- Security: our InfoSec lead (Raj) will require proof of deletion and key rotation policy detail before approving any private deployment. If Redwood can show KMS integration with supported rotation windows, that short-circuits a lot of paperwork.
- Procurement: finance typically needs a commercial term sheet before committing to a PO window. Can you produce a one-page term sheet tied to the pilot pricing?

On timing — we can commit to a security kickoff on 2026-09-07, and finance can start the procurement review the week of 2026-09-14. That should align with a POC start the week of 2026-09-21 if we sign off.

Small ask: could you add a line in the MAP that explicitly lists acceptance criteria we’ll use to evaluate the pilot (latency p95 threshold, manual review reduction %, and a quality threshold for false positives)?

Thanks — will loop in our legal once we have the one-page term sheet.

— Samantha
VP, Program Operations | HealthMatrix

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-31T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Leadership post-call: value hypotheses, procurement path, escalation items

Aditya — quick internal note to confirm roles and the technical approach.
- I’ll take point on SRE onboarding and define the minimal runbook for the POC (health checks, tracing, and sampling).
- Neha — can you prep the legal artifact pack (SOC2 summary, AICPA statements, and a KMS integration checklist) to hand to HealthMatrix legal? Aim to have by 2026-09-04 so we can hit their security kickoff.
- I’ll also draft the one-page term sheet for the pilot and share it as a separate doc (pricing + acceptance criteria).

If folks agree I’ll create the calendar invites and include a 60-min security kickoff and a 90-min POC planning session.

— Marissa
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lewis <samantha.lewis@healthmatrix.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@healthmatrix.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-02T09:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Leadership post-call: value hypotheses, procurement path, escalation items

Thanks all — updated plan attached and a short answers doc inline below. I attached the draft MAP and the security checklist as promised.

Short answers to Samantha’s asks: 
- One-page term sheet: attached (HealthMatrix-draft-MAP.xlsx includes a term sheet tab).
- Acceptance criteria: included as an "Acceptance" sheet in the MAP — p95 latency <= 350ms for the scoped flow, manual-review reduction >= 25% for flagged claims, quality regression detection: false positive delta < 5% vs baseline.
- KMS rotation & deletion: we support customer-managed keys via KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS). Rotation policies can be configured to your windows; we will include proof-of-rotation logs in the audit bundle.

Next steps I’ll execute this week:
- Share the SOC2 redaction bundle and network diagram (Neha).
- Send the one-page term sheet and ask for finance contact to begin procurement paperwork.
- Set calendar invites: security kickoff (2026-09-07) and POC planning (2026-09-21).

If HealthMatrix wants a temporary hosted bridge while KMS gating completes, we can scope that as an alternate option in the term sheet (with additional audit covenants).

— Aditya
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: HealthMatrix-draft-MAP.xlsx (term sheet & acceptance criteria), HealthMatrix-Security-Requirements.pdf (security checklist)
